determinant_shift: Omega_lambda(y) = ((y_1...y_N)/t^{N(N-1)/2})^c Omega_{lambda-c(1^N)}(y); the naive shift omits the t-power and is false already at N=2, lambda=(1,1)
macdonald_coefficient: A = (1+q)(1-t)/(1-qt), from the (q,t) Hall inner product
scope: W_(2,0)(x) - W_(1,1)(x) = (x_1-x_2)^2/(2+A) >= 0, so the 1^n normalization survives
